title: Low-Precision Quality Adapter: unified metric adapters for downstream task fidelity
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: When moving models from FP32/FP16 to low-precision runtimes (FP8/INT8) we observe subtle distributional shifts that break downstream task metrics. Existing metric runners compute raw scores (perplexity, MMLU-style accuracy, ROUGE/BLEU, task-specific scorers) against references without accounting for shift introduced by quantization and calibration. This causes noisy gating decisions and false-positive regressions during canaries and rollouts.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, pluggable Quality Adapter layer that normalizes model outputs for metric computation and exposes per-task fidelity hooks. The adapter should: 1) align output distributions with the reference FP baseline where appropriate (probability-space alignment), 2) support per-task scorers (MMLU, summarization, translation, classification), 3) provide configurable bias-correction for perplexity and confidence-windowed accuracy for classification tasks, and 4) integrate with existing eval-harness and the quant-profile store so thresholds live next to quantization metadata.

Scope: Build metric adapter service + scorer registry + CI/eval pipeline integration and dashboards. Not in scope: retraining or optimizing model weights.

Design summary:
- Adapter layer (metrics-adapter-service): receives model outputs (tokens + logits, optional KV metadata) and a context object containing quant-profile id and target scorer id. The adapter performs probabilistic calibration transforms (temperature scaling, monotonic isotonic calibrator, and a learned alpha scalar for per-token probability-space shrinkage).
- Scorer registry (scorers/registry): plugin registry for task-specific scorers. Each scorer provides a compute(contract) surface: score(input, output, options) -> {score, unit, metadata}. Scorers included initially: perplexity-bias-corrected, mmlu-acc-v2, rouge-l-delta, bleu-sacre-compatible, token-coverage, and a lightweight NER scorer.
- Reference alignment: for perplexity and generation tasks we support an optional inverse-logit mapping that reweights low-precision logits to better match FP baseline token ranking before computing metric. We expose a per-profile alpha parameter stored in quant-profiles DB.
- Thresholding and gating: per-task thresholds and confidence windows are stored in quant-quality profiles. Rollout checkers consult adapter outputs and canary traces to decide pass/fail.

Acceptance criteria:
- Adapter can compute bias-corrected perplexity and MMLU accuracy on test suites with reproducible deltas vs FP baseline (delta < 1% absolute for primary models by default).
- Scorer registry supports hot-plugging a new scorer via a Python interface; a PR demonstrates adding a toy scorer.
- CI job that runs the adapter against a canonical eval set (mmlu+SQuAD+CNN/DM BLEU/ROUGE) produces dashboardable metrics and artifacts (JSON traces).
- Integration tests that exercise rollout gating logic: a canary with quant-profile X either passes or fails deterministically by threshold rules.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Prototype adapter API and scorer registry (week 1-2) - Python package and lightweight HTTP shim to receive model outputs.
2) Integrate one calibration transform (temperature + alpha) and implement perplexity-bias-corrected scorer (week 2-3).
3) Add MMLU-style accuracy scorer and BLEU/ROUGE wrappers that use our tokenizer normalization (week 3-4).
4) Wire profile metadata (alpha, enabled_scorers, thresholds) into quant-profiles DB and add CI eval job (week 4).
5) Dashboard wiring and rollout gating integration with Console (week 5).

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for adapters and scorers in scorers/* with mocked logits.
- Regression suite: run adapter on a small FP baseline and two quantized variants (FP8/INT8) and store result deltas.
- Statistical validation: bootstrap confidence intervals for MMLU and BLEU so canary checks account for sampling noise.
- Performance smoke tests: ensure adapter adds <2ms median overhead for streaming token scoring when deployed as co-located sidecar.

Telemetry & Observability:
- Emit per-request metadata: quant_profile_id, scorer_id, raw_score, adjusted_score, alpha_used, transform_key.
- Aggregate: mean delta from FP baseline, pass/fail counts by profile, metric distribution histograms.
- Dashboards: quant-quality overview, per-model/per-profile fidelity trend, canary timeline.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Overfitting adapter transforms to a small eval set producing brittle thresholds. Mitigation: require multi-dataset validation and guardrails via statistical CI and human review before promoting thresholds.
- Risk: Adapter overhead impacts latency SLOs. Mitigation: allow sidecar vs in-process modes; perf budget enforced in CI.
- Risk: Metrics differ from community baselines (e.g., sacreBLEU). Mitigation: provide compatibility modes that call sacreBLEU/sacreROUGE for canonical comparability and surface differences in metadata.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1: Internal alpha used by research and quantization team to tune alpha parameters for top 5 models.
- Stage 2: Add to dedicated canaries for runtime-1.20 images; expose scores in Console as "quant-quality" panel.
- Stage 3: Default gating for low-risk models; opt-in for high-risk enterprise tenants.

Artifacts & links: [RFC] https://redwood.atlassian.com/confluence/quant-quality-adapter (internal), PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metrics-adapter/pulls, demo runbook: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/evals/quant-alpha-demo, canonical dataset S3: s3://redwood-eval/mmlu/splits/2025-03.

Notes: This ticket focuses on metric correctness and gating ergonomics, not on retraining or changing runtime kernels. The adapter should be backwards-compatible with existing eval-harness outputs and be easy for PM/SE to add new scorers via a documented interface.
updates: 2025-03-13: Kickoff meeting; alignment with ML Research (Iris Zhao) and Product (Sofia Li). Agreed initial metric set: perplexity-bias-corrected, MMLU, ROUGE-L, sacreBLEU, token-coverage.
2025-03-16: Prototype API sketch checked in under metrics-adapter repo; initial scorer registry interface landed (PR #12).
2025-03-18: Experimented with alpha scalar on tyger-2-large: alpha=0.92 reduced perplexity delta from 2.4% -> 0.7% vs FP baseline on CNN/DM small split.
2025-03-20: Review feedback from Design (Marcus Chen): surface adjusted_score and raw_score side-by-side in Console; added metadata fields to telemetry.
2025-03-22: PM requested that sacreBLEU compatibility mode be default for translation tasks to avoid community mismatch — implemented a wrapper.
2025-03-24: Security note from Priya Shah — telemetry should strip PII and prompt text must never be sent to external scoring services; updated privacy checklist.
2025-03-26: Performance smoke test shows adapter adds 1.4ms median for in-process path on CPU-bound scoring; marking performance risk as low.
comments: Sofia Li (PM): Nice progress. For MMLU we need per-task weighting in the future (not part of this ticket). Please add acceptance criterion for CI reproducibility.
Iris Zhao (ML Research): Alpha scalar is promising but we should avoid hand-tuning per-model; propose adding a small calibration job that optimizes alpha on validation split. Add as follow-up.
Marcus Chen (Design): UX note — show sample examples where adapter changed token ranking to help reviewers trust the transform. Add an 'explain' endpoint to the adapter.
Priya Shah (Security): Confirmed no plaintext prompts to external services. Please ensure logs truncate prompt bodies and store only hashed IDs.
